stem: A client has confirmed vitamin B12 deficiency. Which clinical pattern is most consistent with this deficiency?

options.A: Macrocytic or megaloblastic anemia may occur with peripheral neuropathy, ataxia, or loss of proprioception, although neurologic findings can appear without anemia.
options.B: Microcytic anemia is expected, while neurologic findings such as peripheral neuropathy or impaired proprioception are not associated with the deficiency.
options.C: Hypercalcemia and nephrolithiasis are the characteristic findings, while red-cell size and neurologic function are generally unaffected by vitamin B12 deficiency.
options.D: Polycythemia from excessive erythropoiesis is typical, with preserved neurologic function despite reduced vitamin B12 availability and impaired cobalamin metabolism.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance states that vitamin B12 is required for hematopoiesis and normal neuronal function. Deficiency frequently causes macrocytic anemia and neurologic manifestations including peripheral neuropathy, weakness, hyperreflexia, ataxia, loss of proprioception, and poor coordination. Mayo specifically notes that these manifestations may occur in any combination and that many patients have neurologic defects without macrocytic anemia. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize macrocytic/megaloblastic anemia and neurologic dysfunction as important manifestations of vitamin B12 deficiency while understanding that neurologic findings may occur without anemia.
source_version_date: Current Mayo test catalog; live page retrieved 2026-08-26; test-definition document generated May 13, 2026

source_claim_supported: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause macrocytic/megaloblastic anemia and neurologic dysfunction, and neurologic manifestations may occur even without anemia.

correction_summary: Balanced all options as complete clinical patterns and preserved the important nuance that neurologic B12 manifestations can occur without macrocytic anemia.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current Mayo guidance directly lists macrocytic anemia and multiple neurologic manifestations and explicitly states neurologic defects may occur without anemia; A uniquely matches.
